- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates sharp reversals; increase downward bias or add early correction factor.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >80), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged upward trend; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or introduce mean-reversion anchor.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 80+ → 75–78), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias proportional to sentiment volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates late-period spikes (e.g., 88+ in last 5–7 days); add sentiment-weighted tail risk buffer (e.g., +10–15% if sentiment > 0.67).
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.67 → 0.00” transitions, model tends to miss sudden drops; add early warning rule: if sentiment drops below 0.33, reduce forecast by 2–3% per day.
